name: task_create
description:
Create a bash-driven task card. The runtime polls `trigger_script` every `check_interval` seconds; the LAST line of stdout must be `[start]`, `[start] <message>`, or `[skip]`. On `[start]` the agent is activated; the optional `<message>` becomes the seed input. Optional `end_script` is polled while the agent is running and must end with `[done]` (mark card finished) or `[not_done]`. Non-zero exit or unrecognised output is treated as `[skip]` / `[not_done]` (fail-closed) and logged as an error.

Examples — just the trigger_script body:
  * Every hour: `echo [start]` (check_interval=3600)
  * After 9am daily: `[[ $(date +%H) -ge 9 ]] && echo [start] || echo [skip]`
  * When a build flag appears: `[[ -f build/done.flag ]] && echo [start] "build ready" || echo [skip]`
  * One-shot at epoch: `(( $(date +%s) >= 1735689600 )) && echo [start] || echo [skip]`

Scripts land on disk at core/tasks/<name>.trigger.sh and core/tasks/<name>.end.sh; the agent can bash-edit them directly after creation. Agents also have `task_finish` to end cards imperatively.

name.description: Task name (unique per session; used as the filename under core/tasks/).

description.description: What this task should do when it fires. Shown in the wakeup prompt.

check_interval.description: Seconds between trigger_script runs. Defaults to 3600 (1h). Also applied to end_script polling while the card is active.

trigger_script.description: Bash snippet (body only — shebang is prepended). Last line of stdout MUST be `[start]`, `[start] <message>`, or `[skip]`.

end_script.description: Optional bash snippet polled while status=working. Last line must be `[done]` (card finishes) or `[not_done]`.
